title: Hair Salon Scissor Cutting Practice Sheets — Scissor Skills Pack

overview.description: Hair salon themed scissor cutting practice sheets. The child gives haircuts to illustrated faces by cutting along lines of varying difficulty (straight, wavy, zigzag). The hair IS the cutting line — the theme makes the practice purposeful and fun. Second fine motor drop from Aless (after hole punch strips). Both target hand skills: hole punching builds grip strength, scissor cutting builds cutting precision.

themeAsPurpose.description: The cutting line IS the hair. The child is not cutting an abstract line — they are giving a haircut. The theme provides both motivation and a natural error-check (if the hair looks weird, the cut went off track).
themeAsPurpose.value: Purpose-driven fine motor practice. The child is playing hairdresser, not doing a motor skills exercise.

progressiveDifficulty.description: Hair styles progress from straight cuts (easiest) to wavy to zigzag to curly (hardest). Same progressive scaffolding as the Paw Patrol pre-writing pages.
progressiveDifficulty.value: Built-in differentiation. Start with straight cuts, advance to complex curves.

gaps.name: themed-scissor-cutting-page
gaps.description: A page where the cutting line is embedded in a theme (hair for haircuts, grass for mowing, waves for surfing). Progressive difficulty: straight → wavy → zigzag → curves. The theme makes the cutting purposeful — the child is doing something, not just cutting.

notes: Link likely expired. Second fine motor drop (after hole punch strips). Aless values fine motor as its own skill area: hole punching (grip strength) + scissor cutting (precision). Both activities are themed to make practice feel like play. The hair salon theme is particularly clever — the cutting line IS the content.
